confound_assessment: The constraint asymmetry is a genuine cross-model procedural difference and must accompany every strict-vs-GPT comparison: DeepSeek outputs were schema-guaranteed at the wire whereas GPT outputs were schema-validated only by the same tolerant application-level parser used for plain-text tool turns.

Empirically the confound did not produce protocol noise in this run: 0 parse failures / 0 INVALID / 0 AMBIGUOUS across both the 44 json_object decisions and the 66 plain-text tool-turn decisions, so every DA contrast is computed on the full n=110 for both models.

The difference cannot explain the substantive mechanism shift (false-commit-accept 7/8 cells and reduced over-abstention): those are decision-content differences among perfectly parseable ternary outputs, not schema-compliance differences.

Because 66/110 GPT decisions arrived via the model-dependent plain-text tool-turn path, the comparison should be described as 'same frozen runner and parser, provider-specific output enforcement', and a future replication with a provider-neutral strict-schema-compatible decision turn would remove the residual asymmetry.
